findings.problem: Upstream research and formulary records cross Hebrew Psalm 25 verse-half divisions onto Clementine Vulgate Psalm 24, creating a false Vulgate locus and an internal contradiction with the Gradual record: in the bound Clementine Vulgate (ebible-latvuc, 21-psalms.tsv) and Douay-Rheims 1899 (american-1899-ebible, 21-psalms.tsv), Vulgate Ps 24:3 reads 'Neque irrideant me inimici mei:' (v. 3a) 'etenim universi qui sustinent te, non confundentur.' (v. 3b). Because the Introit and Offertory antiphons sing all of Vulgate verse 3 (both 3a and 3b), their Vulgate extent is Ps 24:1-3, 4b (Introit) and Ps 24:1-3 (Offertory) -- matching the 1962 Missal's own printed citation 'Ps. 24, 1-3' and generated/scriptural-date-location.tex -- and the Old Latin reading 'qui te exspectant' replaces Gallican 'qui sustinent te' in Vulgate v. 3b (Heb. 25:3a), NOT v. 3a. Calling the Introit/Offertory 'Ps 24:1-3a' and placing 'qui te exspectant' in 'v. 3a' directly contradicts the records' own Gradual locus 'Ps 24:3b, 4b (Heb. 25:3a, 4)' (research/context.md:75, research/scope.md:53, propers/verified.md:86) for the exact same clause. In addition, the Postcommunion echo Ps 47:10 ('Suscepimus, Deus, misericordiam tuam in medio templi tui') is labeled '(Heb. 48:9)' at research/context.md:81 and propers/verified.md:151, printing modern English 48:9 under the 'Heb.' label instead of Masoretic Hebrew 48:10 (where the superscription is v. 1, matching the records' own convention at Ps 84:8 = 'Heb. 85:8; modern English 85:7' and Ps 84:13 = 'Heb. 85:13; modern English 85:12').

findings.problem: Propagating STU-008 into the reader-facing expansive study, ten citations in sections 01-04 label the Introit and Offertory 'Ps. 24:1--3a, 4b' / 'Ps. 24:1--3a', and two prose sentences explicitly state that the Introit retains Old Latin 'qui te exspectant' in 'v. 3a' (02-appointed-text.tex:7) / 'verse 3a' (03-detailed-commentary.tex:6, rewritten in iteration 1). In the Clementine Vulgate and Douay-Rheims Bible, Ps. 24:3a is 'Neque irrideant me inimici mei:' ('Neither let my enemies laugh at me:') and Ps. 24:3b is 'etenim universi qui sustinent te, non confundentur.' ('for none of them that wait on thee shall be confounded.'). Printing 'Ps. 24:1--3a' for the Introit and Offertory right beside 'Ps. 24:3b' for the Gradual (01:18, 02:40, 02:46, 03:22) misleads readers into thinking the Introit stops before 'qui te exspectant' and contradicts the study's own Gradual citations on the same page, risking propagation onto Page 1 of the upcoming concise study. Likewise, sections/02-appointed-text.tex:106 and sections/03-detailed-commentary.tex:52 label the Postcommunion's Ps. 47:10 echo '(Heb. 48:9)' rather than '(Heb. 48:10; modern English 48:9)', conflicting with the study's Masoretic Hebrew numbering at Ps. 84:8 (Heb. 85:8; modern English 85:7), Ps. 84:13 (Heb. 85:13; modern English 85:12), and Ps. 79:3 (Heb. 80:3).

Update sections/02-appointed-text.tex:106 and sections/03-detailed-commentary.tex:52 from 'Heb.~48:9' to 'Heb.~48:10; modern English 48:9' (or 'Heb.~48:10') consistent with the study's Masoretic numbering elsewhere.

findings.problem: In summarizing St. Thomas Aquinas's Postilla super Psalmos on Ps. 24:4 (Parma Vol. 14, p. 230), sections/06-lane-conversion.tex:22 (following research/interpretations.md:125) writes that the psalmist asks God to show these paths ('ostende eas mihi') 'both to the intellect (under Vias tuas) and to the affections (under Et semitas)'. In the Parma 14 text, however, 'Has vias ego non cognosco; et ideo ostende eas mihi, et quantum ad intellectum, et quantum ad affectum' belongs wholly within the exposition of 'Vias tuas' (the precepts), while the subsequent 'Quantum ad secundum dicit, Et semitas' returns to the outer division of the active life ('communis per praeceptum, specialis per consilia') and expounds 'Et semitas' solely as the narrower footpath of the evangelical counsels without mentioning 'affectus'. Although Parma 14's reportatio creates this surface ambiguity by jumping from 'Quantum ad primum dicitur Isa. 50' straight to 'Quantum ad secundum dicit, Et semitas', assigning 'intellect' to 'Vias tuas' and 'affections' to 'Et semitas' slightly mis-maps Aquinas's division.
findings.required_result: While already editing sections/06-lane-conversion.tex and research/interpretations.md, drop the parenthetical mappings '(under \latin{Vias tuas})' and '(under \latin{Et semitas})' and write 'these ways' instead of 'these paths' -- e.g., 'Because man cannot even discern these ways on his own, the psalmist asks God to show them (\latin{ostende eas mihi}) both to the intellect and to the affections, before turning to the contemplative guidance of verse~5...' -- and align research/interpretations.md:125 accordingly.
